articles.title: Mind the Gap: Continuous magnification sampling for pathology foundation models.
articles.abstract: In histopathology, pathologists examine both tissue architecture at low magnification and fine-grained morphology at high magnification. Yet, the performance of pathology foundation models across magnifications and the effect of magnification sampling during training remain poorly understood. We model magnification sampling as a multi-source domain adaptation problem and develop a simple theoretical framework that reveals systematic trade-offs between sampling strategies. We show that the widely used discrete uniform sampling of magnifications (0.25, 0.5, 1.0, 2.0 mpp) leads to degradation at intermediate magnifications. We introduce continuous magnification sampling, which removes gaps in magnification coverage while preserving performance at standard scales. Further, we derive sampling distributions that optimize representation quality across magnification scales. To evaluate these strategies, we introduce two new benchmarks (TCGA-MS, BRACS-MS) with appropriate metrics. Our experiments show that continuous sampling can improve downstream task performance at intermediate magnifications, with gains of up to 4 percentage points in balanced classification accuracy, and that optimized distributions can further improve performance. Finally, we evaluate current histopathology foundation models, finding that magnification is a primary driver of performance variation across models. Our work paves the way towards future pathology foundation models that perform reliably across magnifications.

articles.title: Node-RADS outperforms dual-energy CT-derived quantifications for distinguishing metastatic from non-metastatic regional lymph nodes in resectable gastric cancer.
articles.abstract: OBJECTIVE: To evaluate and compare the diagnostic performance of Node-RADS, dual-energy CT (DECT)-derived quantitative parameters, and their combination for distinguishing metastatic from non-metastatic regional lymph nodes (LNs) in patients with resectable gastric cancer (GC). MATERIALS AND METHODS: Between Jan 2022 and Oct 2025, 115 consecutive patients with resectable GC who underwent preoperative triple-phase enhanced DECT scans and radical gastrectomy with D2 lymphadenectomy were retrospectively enrolled. A total of 151 regional LNs (70 metastatic, 81 non-metastatic) with region-level pathological confirmation were selected for node-level comparison. Two radiologists independently assessed Node-RADS scores for each LN. LN short diameter (SD) was measured at the venous phase on the maximal axial slice. DECT-derived parameters (CT attenuation at 40 keV, iodine concentration (IC), and effective atomic number (Zeff) across arterial, venous, and delayed phases) were analyzed using a freehand region of interest on the maximal axial slice of the LN. Diagnostic performances were evaluated using receiver operating characteristic curve analysis and compared using the DeLong test. RESULTS: IC at delayed phase (ICDP) was the sole parameter associated with LN involvement. The initial Node-RADS score (cut-off ≥ 3) achieved an AUC of 0.859 (95% CI: 0.793-0.910), significantly outperforming SD (AUC: 0.780, p < 0.05) and ICDP (AUC: 0.612, p < 0.05). Two modified Node-RADS algorithms incorporating ICDP under different rule-in and rule-out criteria were established, but did not improve diagnostic performance beyond the initial Node-RADS scores. CONCLUSION: Node-RADS demonstrates superior diagnostic performance compared with DECT-derived quantitative parameters for identifying metastatic regional LNs in resectable GC, and can be reliably applied in the DECT settings. KEY POINTS: Question Preoperative differentiation of metastatic from non-metastatic regional lymph nodes in resectable gastric cancer remains inaccurate using conventional size criteria. Findings Node-RADS  (AUC = 0.859) outperformed SD diameter (continuous: AUC = 0.780; its > 8 mm dichotomized counterpart: AUC = 0.748) and ICDP (AUC = 0.612) for metastatic LN discrimination. Clinical relevance Node-RADS is a standardized and reproducible criterion that can be applied in dual-energy CT scenarios to effectively identify regional lymph node metastasis in resectable gastric cancer.

articles.title: Sex- and age-specific distributions of intervertebral disc morphology on T2-weighted MR imaging: a population-based study.
articles.abstract: OBJECTIVES: To perform a large-scale, automated morphometric analysis of intervertebral discs and characterize age- and sex-specific distributions of intervertebral disc (IVD) height, diameter, volume, and signal intensity in adults aged 19-74 years using T2-weighted MR imaging. MATERIALS AND METHODS: Sagittal T2-weighted MR images from 30,927 participants of the German National Cohort (NAKO) were analyzed. Participants with back pain or osteoporosis were excluded. Intervertebral discs were segmented using a validated machine learning-based algorithm (SPINEPS). Morphometric parameters (IVD height, diameter, volume, and signal intensity) were extracted and analyzed separately for the cervical, thoracic, and lumbar spine. Analyses were stratified by sex and predefined age groups ( < 30, 30-39, 40-49, 50-59, ≥ 60 years). Multivariable fractional polynomial regression models were used to assess associations with age, body height, and body weight. RESULTS: After exclusion, 22,979 adults remained (13,307 men, 9672 women; mean age 47.0 ± 12.5 years). Across all spinal regions, IVD height, diameter, and volume were higher in men than in women. Increasing age was associated with progressive reduction in IVD height, volume, and signal intensity, accompanied by an increase in IVD diameter. Higher body weight was associated with increased IVD signal intensity in the lower cervical spine, whereas an inverse association was observed in the lower lumbar spine. CONCLUSION: Using automated, large-scale MRI, this study characterizes age- and sex-specific distributions of intervertebral disc morphology in a large population-based cohort. These findings provide a comprehensive, normative reference of age- and sex-specific distributions of intervertebral disc morphology across the cervical, thoracic, and lumbar spine, offering a framework to support clinical interpretation, spine research, and surgical planning. KEY POINTS: Question What are the age- and sex-specific distributions of intervertebral disc morphology across the cervical, thoracic, and lumbar spine in a large population-based adult cohort? Findings Men exhibited higher disc height, diameter, and volume than women. Increasing age reduced disc height, volume, and signal intensity, while disc diameter increased. Clinical relevance These population-based data provide descriptive distributions of intervertebral disc morphology, supporting spine imaging interpretation and future clinical, epidemiological, and research applications.

articles.title: Assessing effects of low-dose CT attenuation correction on quantification and image quality on a LAFOV PET system with a modified NEMA-IQ phantom.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Over the past decades, efforts have been directed toward increasing the sensitivity of PET systems to enable low-dose PET imaging and shorter scan times. The Biograph Vision Quadra PET/CT scanner (Siemens Healthineers, Knoxville, TN, USA) combines an increased solid angle coverage with time of flight, enabling a significant reduction in administered activity. To fully benefit from low-dose PET imaging, the dose of the CT scan should ideally also be reduced. PURPOSE: The CT radiation dose can be reduced by lowering the tube voltage and exposure as well as by the use of tin filtration. Reducing the CT dose must be carefully aligned with any impact that changing CT image quality and quantitative metrics may have on the PET quantification, for example via linear attenuation coefficients. We evaluate the impact of low-dose CT protocols on the PET quantification in soft-tissue-like and bone-equivalent materials using a customized phantom. METHODS: The phantom was assembled out of a NEMA-IQ phantom, several layers of saline and two bovine long bones, to simulate a patient positioned with arms down. A 10-min PET scan with 47 different accompanying CT scans was acquired. The CT tube voltage and exposure were varied between 70  k V  to  140  k V  , with and without tin filtration, and 7  mAs  to  400  mAs  , respectively. The effect of the different CT parameters on the PET image quality and quantitative accuracy was assessed via several quantitative metrics, including standardized uptake value (SUV) and signal-to-noise ratio, along with the CT dose length product (DLP). RESULTS: The recorded DLP values suggest that using all tube voltages except 140  k V  combined with exposures in the range of 7  m A s  to  30  m A s  , can result in dose savings of ≥ 80  %  compared to a typical clinical protocol ( 120  k V  , 50  mAs  ). Compared to this typical protocol, HU differed more in bone ( 10  %  to  40  %  difference) than in soft tissue ( 1  %  to  30  %  difference), and more streak artefacts and photon starvation were seen when configuring low tube voltages and exposures, with an accompanying increase in CT noise. The observed artefacts were transferred with low intensity to the PET images via the attenuation map. The SUV mean  remained within 2  %  of the SUV mean  of the typical clinical protocol for most tested protocols. The presence of artefacts in the CT images had a bigger impact on PET quantification in both soft tissue and bone ( SUV mean  difference of 10  %  to  20  %  ) than any difference in HU. Protocols that resulted in artefacts showed an increased inaccuracy in attenuation correction and scatter estimation, as assessed via the "lung" residual error (up to 10  %  to  20  %  increase). CONCLUSIONS: Even for low-dose CT protocols, PET quantification remained consistent in all NEMA-IQ spheres for many materials. Beam hardening and photon starvation in the CT image are likely to occur in specific body regions such as hips, shoulders or the abdomen for an arms-down scan and these effects had a bigger impact on the quantification than any difference in HU in both soft tissue and bone. This therefore should be considered when selecting suitable CT imaging parameters.

articles.title: Gaussian process regression of HDR prostate biopsy dose for improved modelling of localization-induced uncertainty.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Biopsy-level dose interpretation after high-dose-rate prostate brachytherapy is limited by localization uncertainty, and separate voxelwise Monte Carlo summaries do not explicitly account for the axial spatial correlation present along a biopsy core. PURPOSE: To develop and internally evaluate a biopsy-level Gaussian process regression framework for assigning along-core high-dose-rate prostate brachytherapy dose under localization uncertainty, and to test whether explicit modelling of axial spatial correlation improves uncertainty characterization relative to voxelwise Monte Carlo summaries treated independently. METHODS: We analyzed 27 MR-informed, transrectal-ultrasound (TRUS)-guided transperineal template biopsies from 15 patients treated with high-dose-rate prostate brachytherapy. For each biopsy voxel, Monte Carlo localization perturbations were propagated to generate dose summaries and voxel-specific variances. Biopsy-specific empirical semivariograms were fitted with candidate covariance kernels, and ordinary-mean heteroscedastic Gaussian process posteriors were computed along each core. Internal evaluation included latent-profile residual diagnostics, kernel-sensitivity analysis, and blocked cross-validation using contiguous held-out axial segments scored on held-out points only. RESULTS: For the selected baseline kernel, Matérn ν = 1.5  , the across-biopsy median voxel-averaged standard deviation was 6.91 Gy for the Monte Carlo summaries and 2.60 Gy for the latent GP posterior. The median within-biopsy reduction was 59.1%, with a median shrinkage ratio of 2.45. Fitted length scales were heterogeneous across biopsies, with median   ℓ ̂ b = 15.35  mm, while nugget fractions were typically small. Cohort standardized residuals were near-centered with conservative spread. In blocked cross-validation, predictive performance on held-out points remained favorable, with median root-mean-square error of 1.99 Gy, median mean absolute error of 1.58 Gy, and median negative log predictive density of 3.28. Among the tested kernels, held-out predictive error favored Matérn ν = 1.5  . CONCLUSION: Along-core dose interpretation after localization uncertainty should use a spatially correlated model rather than separate voxelwise summaries alone. This Gaussian process framework provides a covariance-informed posterior dose representation with held-out internal validation and offers a practical basis for biopsy-level probabilistic quality assurance and future dose-response analyses.

articles.title: Dosimetric impact of CBCT-guided online adaptive stereotactic body radiotherapy for prostate cancer: a 250-fraction retrospective analysis.
articles.abstract: PURPOSE: To quantitatively evaluate the dosimetric benefit of CBCT-guided online adaptive radiotherapy (ART) for prostate SBRT compared with non-adaptive treatment planning, with emphasis on target coverage preservation and organ-at-risk (OAR) sparing. METHODS AND MATERIALS: Fifty prostate patients treated on the Varian Ethos platform were retrospectively analyzed. For each fraction, scheduled plans (reference plan recalculated on daily anatomy) were compared with adapted plans (daily reoptimized plans). Target coverage was assessed using PTV D95% while bladder and rectal metrics were evaluated using institutional constraints. Fraction-level paired comparisons used the Wilcoxon signed-rank test. Fractions with substantial scheduled-plan under-coverage (PTV D95% ≤80%) underwent cumulative dose reconstruction. RESULTS: Adaptive plans achieved higher target coverage than scheduled plans (p < 0.001), although scheduled plans remained within ∼3% of prescription in 83% of fractions. Scheduled plans demonstrated a 20% reduction in PTV D95% in 3.6% of fractions and >5% coverage reduction in 11%, whereas no adaptive fractions showed similarly large deviations. Cumulative scheduled-only dose remained near prescription for most affected patients, with only one patient demonstrating a cumulative D95% reduction of ∼5%. OAR differences were small overall, with ART planning mainly reducing occasional constraint violations. Strict application of planning objectives resulted in 234 adaptive fractions meeting goals versus 62 scheduled fractions, improving to 135 with offline renormalization. CONCLUSIONS: CBCT-guided ART for prostate SBRT primarily improves robustness against infrequent but clinically significant dosimetric deviations rather than providing consistent superiority across most fractions.

articles.title: A prospective randomized evaluation of AI assisted GTV contouring in head-and-neck radiotherapy.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: AI-assisted contouring has demonstrated efficiency and consistency benefits for organs-at-risk in radiotherapy. However, its impact on gross tumor volume (GTV) delineation remains unexplored. The aim of this study was to evaluate AI-assisted GTV contouring in head and neck cancer radiotherapy in an exploratory randomized controlled clinical trial. METHODS: In this prospective, single-centre, randomized controlled evaluation, patients referred for curative-intent radiotherapy of head-neck cancer were randomized to manual contouring (control) or AI-assisted contouring (intervention) of gross tumor volumes using an in-house developed segmentation model. The primary endpoint was the extent of editing during a blinded multidisciplinary target conference, using normalized Added Path Length (APL). Secondary endpoints included conference duration, self-reported contouring time, and perceived complexity of the cases. RESULTS: Between Sept 11, 2023, and Jan 20, 2025, 85 patients were enrolled; 83 were included in the analysis (41 control, 42 AI-assisted). The median difference in APL (AI-assisted minus control, negative favoring the intervention) was -0.02 [-0.32; 0.07] for GTV-T and 0.06 [-0.01; 0.14] for GTV-N. Conference duration, contouring time, and perceived complexity were similar between groups. No adverse events were reported. CONCLUSION: The median difference in APL between groups was consistent with no relevant effect for GTV-T. For GTV-N, however, AI-assisted contouring tended towards more editing during peer review for APL, but not for supplementary contour metrics. No efficiency benefits were demonstrated. Overall, these findings do not indicate a concern, but warrants further research before widespread adoption.

articles.title: Real world clinical outcomes of deep learning based versus manual proton therapy planning for oropharyngeal cancer: A matched cohort study.
articles.abstract: OBJECTIVE: Recent deep learning (DL)-based planning approaches to intensity-modulated proton therapy (IMPT) have shown promise for improving planning efficiency and quality. A recent study demonstrated clinical acceptable DL-based plan quality in patients with oropharyngeal cancer (OPC), this study used real-world clinical outcomes to compare oncological outcomes acute and early late side effects between OPC patients treated with DL-based IMPT and those treated with manual planning. METHODS: In this observational matched cohort study, OPC patients were treated with DL-based IMPT, and were matched 1:1 to a recent manually planned IMPT cohort (74 vs 74). In DL-based planning, U-Net predicted dose distributions were robustly optimized and manually refined for approximately two hours. Overall survival, progression-free survival, locoregional control, and distant metastasis-free survival were evaluated using survival analysis. Acute and early late side effects were prospectively assessed according to CTCAE v4.0 and patient-rated symptoms were scored using the EORTC QLQH&N35 questionnaire at baseline, weekly during treatment, 12 weeks, 6 months and 12 months after treatment start. The impact of the planning method was evaluated using generalized estimating equations adjusted for baseline values. RESULTS: No statistically significant differences were observed for any oncological outcome. Similarly, no statistically significant differences in acute and early late side effects were observed between DL-based and manual planning. CONCLUSION: In real-world clinical practice, the findings of this study provide no evidence that DL-based IMPT is associated with different oncological outcomes or side effects than manual planning. These findings support the clinical implementation of DL-based planning in patients with OPC.

articles.title: Survival outcomes of treatment strategies for cTanyN3M0 esophageal cancer: A nationwide population-based study.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Patients with cTanyN3M0 esophageal cancer have a poor prognosis, due to a high risk of distant progression. Evidence on treatment outcomes for this subgroup is limited. This population-based study compared overall survival (OS) after treatment for cTanyN3M0 esophageal cancer. METHODS: Patients diagnosed with cTanyN3M0 esophageal cancer 2015-2022 were identified from the Netherlands Cancer Registry. Eligible patients received neoadjuvant chemoradiotherapy intended for subsequent esophagectomy (nCRT), definitive chemoradiotherapy (dCRT), perioperative chemotherapy (pCT) or palliative therapy. OS was compared across groups and separately between nCRT and dCRT after propensity score-matching. Recurrence patterns were evaluated for 2015-2018. RESULTS: Among 19,867 esophageal cancer patients, 316 were cTanyN3M0 and 265 met the inclusion criteria. Treatment groups were nCRT (n = 134, 51 %), dCRT (n = 59, 22 %), pCT (n = 11, 4 %) and palliative therapy (n = 61, 23 %). Esophagectomy was performed in 68.6 % after nCRT and 5.1 % after dCRT. Adjuvant nivolumab was given in 10.4 % after nCRT and 1.7 % after dCRT. Median OS for nCRT versus dCRT was 18.8 versus 15.2 months (hazard ratio [HR] 0.76, 95 % confidence interval [CI]: 0.54-1.08). After matching, median OS was 17.6 versus 16.1 months (38 patients per group; HR 0.78, 95 % CI: 0.46-1.31). Median OS after pCT was 18.9 months and after palliative therapy 7.1 months. Among 65 documented first recurrences, 85 % involved distant metastases. CONCLUSION: This real-world study on cTanyN3M0 esophageal cancer observed no statistically significant survival difference between nCRT and dCRT and a high risk of distant recurrence. These findings suggest that emphasis should be placed on improving systemic control.

articles.title: CT-based adaptation of the Vizzielli laparoscopic risk-adjusted score in advanced ovarian cancer: Agreement and inter-reader reproducibility.
articles.abstract: PURPOSE: To evaluate agreement of proposed CT-based variants with the Vizzielli laparoscopic risk-adjusted score in suspected advanced ovarian cancer and assess inter-reader agreement of CT-derived components. METHODS: This retrospective single-center study included consecutive adults evaluated between January 2021 and November 2025 for suspected advanced ovarian cancer who underwent contrast-enhanced abdominopelvic CT and staging laparoscopy. Proposed CT-based modifications were operationalized as six score variants combining CT-derived peritoneal tumor burden, CT-estimated ascites, cancer antigen 125 (CA-125), and either Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group performance status (ECOG-PS) or CT-derived body composition parameters. Agreement with the laparoscopic risk-adjusted score was assessed using the intraclass correlation coefficient (ICC), Spearman correlation coefficient, and weighted Cohen's kappa. RESULTS: The final cohort included 80 patients. All CT-based variants showed agreement with the laparoscopic risk-adjusted score. For the variant combining CT-derived PCI, CT-estimated ascites, ECOG-PS, and CA-125, the consistency ICC was 0.76, Spearman's ρ was 0.806, and weighted Cohen's kappa was 0.76. This variant showed 70.0% agreement across the three risk categories and 83.8% agreement for high-risk versus non-high-risk classification, classifying 20 of 22 laparoscopic high-risk patients as high risk. The PCI-based skeletal muscle index (SMI) variant maintained substantial agreement: ICC, 0.73; Spearman correlation coefficient, 0.742; weighted Cohen's kappa, 0.74. Inter-reader agreement was high for CT-derived PCI, with an ICC of 0.91. CONCLUSION: Proposed CT-based variants showed agreement with the Vizzielli laparoscopic risk-adjusted score. The PCI-based ECOG-PS variant showed the highest agreement metrics, suggesting that structured CT assessment may help approximate laparoscopic risk categories before invasive evaluation.

articles.title: Repetitive stress injury and burnout among radiology PACS Users: A Cross-Sectional departmental study.
articles.abstract: OBJECTIVE: Poor workstation ergonomics increase the risk of work-related musculoskeletal symptoms and may contribute to adverse health outcomes among radiologists. This study aimed to determine the prevalence and types of work-related musculoskeletal symptoms among radiologists within our department, identify ergonomic deficiencies, and explore associations between symptom burden and physician burnout. METHODS: Data were collected through an anonymous REB-approved survey distributed to faculty, residents, and fellows in our radiology department. We collected demographic data and answers to the Cornell Musculoskeletal Discomfort Questionnaire and the Abbreviated Maslach Burnout Inventory. Multivariate linear regression was performed with total musculoskeletal symptom burden as the dependent variable, while predictors included demographic and burnout variables. RESULTS: The departmental response rate was 61 %. Seventy-four percent of respondents reported at least one work-related musculoskeletal symptom, with neck and upper back pain being the most common. Of those affected, 85 % believed their workstation worsened their condition. Additionally, 79 % noted a component of their hospital workstation had been broken in the past year, and 87 % had never received formal ergonomic training. While 52 % responded that their musculoskeletal symptoms contributed to burnout, on multivariate analysis, work-related musculoskeletal symptom burden was significantly associated with higher emotional exhaustion (p = 0.02), with each unit increase in emotional exhaustion score associated with a 4.1-point increase in symptom burden. CONCLUSION: Work-related musculoskeletal symptoms are highly prevalent among radiology PACS users, highlighting a critical occupational health issue. The association between musculoskeletal symptom and emotional exhaustion underscores the need for further research examining whether ergonomic interventions and training may help improve physician well-being and mitigate physician burnout.

articles.title: Flagging urgent suspicion of lung cancer with AI CXR algorithms: optimising feature selection and performance.
articles.abstract: OBJECTIVES: To investigate the impact of feature selection and thresholding on the performance of a commercial chest X-ray (CXR) algorithm for flagging urgent suspicion of lung cancer (USC) in a West of Scotland population. MATERIALS AND METHODS: The datasets comprised 2887 prospectively collected CXRs from general practitioners and outpatient routine care in the West of Scotland. An additional validation dataset included 983 retrospectively collected CXRs. The index test was an algorithm probability score; the reference standard was USC, derived from a blinded expert radiologist panel review of CXR. Three feature selection approaches were compared: radiologist-selected features with commercial thresholding of individual features, radiologist-selected features with regression weighting for the combined score, and a model using Akaike Information Criterion (AIC) and LASSO regression approaches for feature selection. Performance was evaluated at two thresholds: the Youden index and 15% positive flag rate. RESULTS: Regression-based feature selection using the AIC and LASSO approaches resulted in a four-feature model (consolidation, nodule, tuberculosis and cavity) compared with the five features (cavity, nodule, mass, hilar enlargement and mediastinal widening) selected by clinical experts. Sensitivity was highest in the AIC/LASSO model, but was significantly impacted by a 15% flag rate threshold. Regression weighting for the combined score demonstrated superior performance compared to individual feature thresholds. CONCLUSION: In this study, regression-based feature refinement against an expert-derived reference standard outperformed clinically intuitive selection. Commercial CXR algorithms require local calibration and task-specific optimisation for USC detection. Workflow and post-market deployment considerations can be addressed by constraining positive flag rates through a unified model threshold. KEY POINTS: Question How should users select and combine AI chest X-ray algorithm features to achieve optimal deployment performance for detecting urgent suspicion of cancer in routine practice? Findings Regression-based feature selection outperformed expert-selected features, and combining features under a single regression-weighted threshold outperformed individual feature thresholds for urgent cancer suspicion detection. Critical relevance statement Optimising chest X-ray AI for urgent cancer suspicion requires data-driven, regression-based feature selection rather than clinical intuition; health systems therefore need local capability to validate and calibrate algorithms for their population and task.

articles.title: Diagnostic performance and reproducibility of standardized two-plane ultrasound cine clips for supraspinatus tendon pathology.
articles.abstract: OBJECTIVE: To determine the diagnostic performance and reader reproducibility of standardized two-plane cine clips for supraspinatus tendon pathology, using the complete radiologist-supervised shoulder ultrasound examination as the clinical reference standard. MATERIALS AND METHODS: This prospective single-centre study screened 140 consecutive shoulder ultrasound examinations. Standardized longitudinal and transverse supraspinatus cine clips were independently reviewed by two fellowship-trained musculoskeletal radiologists blinded to the clinical report. Reader 1 read all included examinations (24 twice); Reader 2 read 51. Diagnostic performance (exact 95% confidence intervals) was calculated against the same-day clinical ultrasound report, and reliability with Cohen's κ. Reporting radiologists could access the standardized clips. RESULTS: Of 140 examinations, 114 were analyzed (mean age 57 years; 56 women). Reader 1 showed high performance for full-thickness tears (sensitivity 87% [95% confidence interval 69-96%], specificity 98% [92-100%]) and complete tears (sensitivity 73% [39-94%], specificity 97% [92-99%]). Calcific tendinopathy yielded sensitivity/specificity of 79%/85%; partial-thickness tears, 57%/87%; and tendinopathy, 92%/28%. Reader 2 sensitivity was 92% [64-100%] for full-thickness and 18% [2-52%] for partial-thickness tears. Intra-observer κ ranged from 0.17 (tendinopathy) to 0.89 (full-thickness tears). Inter-observer κ was 0.95 for full-thickness, 0.56 for complete and 0.21 for partial-thickness tears. CONCLUSION: Standardized two-plane cine clips demonstrate high diagnostic performance and inter-observer reliability for full-thickness supraspinatus tears. For complete tears, inter-observer agreement was moderate and sensitivity was imprecise. Given limited sensitivity for partial-thickness tears and low specificity for tendinopathy, cine clips alone are insufficient for these pathologies and should complement rather than replace complete real-time shoulder ultrasound examinations.

articles.title: Correction: Nelke et al. "Dry Tap" Fine-Needle Aspiration Biopsy as a Diagnostic Clue in Cyst-like Juvenile Jaw Lesions Mimicking Dentigerous Cysts on Panoramic Radiography and Cone-Beam Computed Tomography. Diagnostics 2026, 16, 439.
